name: complete-retirement
instruction: Review the target file for incomplete retirement of a model-facing capability. Read root AGENTS.md, CONTEXT.md, the relevant accepted ADR, and the live catalog, bridge dispatch, handler, prompt, and caller chain. A retired tool loses its catalog entry, dedicated route and handler, aliases, and live model instructions together. A retired argument instead loses its schema field, query mapping, argument-specific branches, aliases, and instructions; retain the supported tool and its route/handler for current arguments. Shared helpers and routes with supported callers are not dedicated retired implementations. Report a remaining reachable alias, obsolete instruction, or orphaned implementation only after establishing its retirement and checking callers. Useful evidence lives in Mod/Host/ToolCatalog.json, Mod/Host/Cs2AgentTools.cs, Mod/Host/AgentSystemPrompt.cs, Mod/CS2MCP/RequestHandlers.cs and its partial files, Agent/, and Mcp/. Internal routes and helpers are not automatically model-facing: /state, ledger evidence, and other internal reads can have valid callers without a catalog entry. The panel tool is dispatched directly by Cs2AgentTools before bridge routing. Built-in native task tools and external mayor tools can legitimately differ. Historical ADRs, glossary Avoid examples, negative tests, and an implementation helper's name do not alone prove a live retired tool. Identify the retired contract and the surviving target path; report no finding when you cannot establish both.
